events.title: DEC PDP-1 introduced
events.summary: Digital Equipment Corporation delivered the first PDP-1 to BBN in November 1960 — the first commercial computer with a monitor and keyboard for interactive use.
events.about: The PDP-1 brought real-time interaction to a $120,000 [minicomputer]: a [CRT] display, light pen, and paper-tape I/O. [MIT] hackers built early text tools, debuggers, and [time-sharing] experiments on it — the culture that later produced Unix, the [ARPANET], and personal computing.

narrative.whyChosen: The PDP-1 was the first mass-produced interactive [minicomputer] with a screen and keyboard.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved small machines could support live programming, not just batch jobs.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers needed affordable interactive access instead of queueing decks on room-sized mainframes.
